run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-17T22:08:32Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is backed by its own spans: frontend-proxy ingress error spans (http.status_code 504, error=true, otel.status_code=ERROR, ~15.0 s each) rise from 0–0.02/s before 22:09 to ~1.7–2.2/s from 22:09 to at least 22:17, while its ingress span rate at the same time drops from ~15/s to ~5.4/s. The proxy's own access log shows these as '504 UT response_timeout' after 15000 ms, so the proxy is timing out waiting for the frontend, not failing on its own. The cart service logs 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' from 22:09:05 onward, its Redis client spans (HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE) disappear, its completed gRPC spans take longer than the 15 s bucket, and frontend/checkout show their own error spans on CartService calls. That makes cart's Redis backend valkey-cart the deepest failing dependency observed: the valkey-cart pod is Running with 0 restarts and no probes, has very small limits (cpu 10m, memory 10Mi), and is on the same node as the cart pod with no NetworkPolicy and all nodes Ready. Why valkey-cart stopped answering could not be observed (no valkey logs, no cAdvisor/kube-state-metrics series, no change history), and no alert rule named RequestErrorRate was found, so the conclusion is partial and no flag-based fault injection is supported (all flagd flags are off).

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress spans: STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate was 0–0.022/s from 21:49 to 22:07, then 1.70/s at 22:09 and 2.13–2.23/s through 22:17; over the same points the ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate fell from ~15.1/s to ~5.3–5.5/s.

The frontend-proxy error spans in the sampled view are operation 'ingress' with status tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR" and durations between 14,999,537 and 15,012,202 us (10 such rows in span_groups).

frontend-proxy access log lines between 22:14:30.910Z and 22:14:55.612Z record '504 UT response_timeout' with 15000/14999 ms for 'GET /api/cart', 'POST /api/cart' and 'POST /api/checkout' with upstream 'frontend'.

Trace a545ba7815ee3f559a6bbcc06809bf79 shows load-generator user_view_cart 15.003 s -> load-generator GET 15.0025 s (504) -> frontend-proxy ingress 15.0012 s (504, error) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' 15.0009 s (error="true", http.status_code="0") -> frontend GET 14.9993 s with http.status_code 200: the proxy gave up at its 15 s timeout while the frontend span also spanned ~15 s.

Cart pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7 logs 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' from 22:09:05.338852Z onward (68 matching lines, last seen 22:15:08.241178Z), and each such line is immediately followed by 'Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised.'

Cart's own Redis client spans stop: HGET fell from ~6.82–7.26/s (21:51–22:07) to 1.08/s at 22:09 and 0 from 22:11; HMSET/EXPIRE fell from ~3.3/s to 0; cart gRPC server spans GetCart/AddItem/EmptyCart UNSET rates fell to 0 while 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'AddItem' STATUS_CODE_ERROR series appear from 22:11 (0.068–0.178/s).

Completed cart 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' spans after 22:13 are slower than the largest finite bucket: at 22:18 and 22:23 the le="15000.0" rate is 0 while the +Inf rate is 0.0646/s and 0.0439/s, i.e. the recorded cart spans lasted longer than 15 s.

frontend's own spans carry errors tied to the cart dependency: 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' STATUS_CODE_ERROR appear from 22:11 (0.078–0.178/s), together with 'POST /api/cart', 'GET /api/cart', 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' and 'POST /api/checkout' errors through 22:17.

checkout shows its own errors on cart calls: 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' STATUS_CODE_ERROR appear at the 22:19 sample (0.0112/s) while checkout's cart/payment/currency call rates drop to 0.

The cart pod's configured Redis address is VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379; the valkey-cart Service endpoints resolve to pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr at 100.96.2.228:6379 on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae, and the cart pod (100.96.2.233) is on the same node.

valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr is phase Running, all pod conditions True (including Ready), container ready=true, restartCount=0, lastState empty, started 21:35:29Z; the pod has no livenessProbe, readinessProbe or startupProbe and container resources limits cpu=10m, memory=10Mi (requests cpu=2m, memory=4Mi). The cart container likewise has no probes, restartCount=0, running since 21:35:31Z.

The cart, frontend, frontend-proxy and valkey-cart Deployments each report readyReplicas=1/availableReplicas=1 with condition MinimumReplicasAvailable True; all 21 otel-demo pods were Running with 0 restarts at query time.

The flagd-config ConfigMap holds every fault-related flag at defaultVariant 'off', including cartFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, emailMemoryLeak, imageSlowLoad, kafkaQueueProblems, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure and recommendationCacheFailure.

Cluster events in otel-demo during the window are limited to a pod that no longer exists: Pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s shows 30 'FailedKillPod' warnings ('failed to "KillContainer" for "cart" ... DeadlineExceeded') and 75 'Killing' events, last timestamps 22:11:21Z and 22:11:22Z; the current cart ReplicaSet is cart-755465879b.

The proxy's errors are 504 'UT response_timeout' at exactly 15000 ms logged by frontend-proxy itself, and the corresponding traces contain frontend server spans for the same requests, so the errors come from an upstream (frontend/cart) that did not answer within the envoy timeout rather than from frontend-proxy's own failure or a missing frontend.

No NetworkPolicy exists in otel-demo, all five nodes report Ready/KubeletReady, and all three kube-system CoreDNS pods are Running with restartCount 0, so no cluster-level or policy-level cause is visible for the connectivity loss; cart and valkey-cart are co-located on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae.

flagd-driven fault injection (e.g. cartFailure) is rejected as the cause: the flagd-config ConfigMap keeps cartFailure and all other fault flags on 'off', and the cart pod's own log attributes the failure to Redis connectivity ('Wasn't able to connect to redis'), not to a flag-driven gRPC rejection.

Primary hypothesis: the valkey-cart Redis backend stopped accepting/serving connections from the cart pod at ~22:09:05, so cart's GetCart/AddItem handlers block until the caller's 15 s deadline, the frontend's /api/cart and /api/checkout requests never answer within frontend-proxy's 15 s route timeout, and the proxy emits 504 responses whose error spans raise RequestErrorRate.

Secondary hypothesis for why valkey-cart stopped serving: the container is alive but resource-starved or wedged, consistent with its extremely low limits (cpu 10m, memory 10Mi) combined with the absence of any probe, so Kubernetes cannot detect its unresponsiveness; restartCount 0 and an empty lastState argue against an OOMKill or restart as the mechanism, and CPU throttling cannot be measured because no cAdvisor/kube-state-metrics series are scraped.

Remaining candidate not excluded: the loss is in the network path between the cart pod and the valkey-cart Service/ClusterIP (cart only reports 'Wasn't able to connect to redis'), which would look the same from cart's side even though both pods are on the same node and no NetworkPolicy exists.

Human follow-up: test valkey-cart reachability directly (e.g. redis-cli PING against valkey-cart:6379 from a debug pod on i-0146cb0d0caf26bae), inspect the valkey-cart container's CFS throttling and memory usage with cAdvisor metrics, and add readiness/liveness probes to valkey-cart; if it is genuinely unable to serve, restarting the valkey-cart pod would restore cart and clear the proxy 504s.

gaps: No Prometheus rule named RequestErrorRate was returned by list_prometheus_rules in this window, so the alert's exact expression, lookback and which metric it reads could not be verified.

kube-state-metrics/cAdvisor series are absent from this Prometheus: get_metric_names for {__name__=~"kube_.*"} returned nothing, so valkey-cart/cart CPU throttling, memory usage and container state counts cannot be measured.

The valkey-cart container wrote no log lines in the window, so its internal error state (connection refused vs. hung, resource starvation, block on fork/persistence) is unknown; it has no probes, so 'Ready' does not prove it served requests.
The pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s named in the FailedKillPod/Killing events no longer exists; its node, container last state and relation to the 22:09 failure could not be read.
The change_history integration is not integrated, so what changed at ~22:09:05 (and whether anything was changed in valkey-cart/cart configuration or node state) cannot be determined.
The frontend container returned no log lines for the window, so frontend-side error text could not be read; frontend impact rests on its error spans and the proxy access log only.
Trace span counts are a biased sample and the traces view was truncated at the requested limit, so no complete call graph or exact error rate for unobserved requests is claimed.
Prometheus samples for these trace series only start at 21:49:00, so no earlier baseline than 21:49–22:08 was available.
next_steps: Check valkey-cart responsiveness and CPU throttling from inside the cluster (redis-cli PING, container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total) and consider raising its cpu/memory limits (currently 10m/10Mi) and adding readiness/liveness probes.
Review frontend-proxy's 15 s route timeout and the alert threshold/expression for RequestErrorRate, since all sampled proxy errors are 504 response_timeout at exactly 15000 ms.

Verify whether any configuration or platform change coincided with 22:09:05Z via the (currently unavailable) change-history integration, and inspect the node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae container runtime for the stuck cart container referenced by the FailedKillPod event.
